traceability.evidence:
Core implementation and tests: - Plugin entry point: src/index.ts - Exports default `plugin` object plus named exports `{ rules, configs, maintenance }`. - Dynamically loads rule modules from `./rules/${name}` with graceful error handling. - Defines flat-config-style presets: - `configs.recommended = [ { rules: { 'traceability/require-story-annotation': 'error', ... } } ]` - `configs.strict` mirrors `recommended`. - Annotated with story traceability for this spec: - `@story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md` - `@req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE`, `@req REQ-ERROR-HANDLING`.
- Basic plugin structure tests: - tests/plugin-setup.test.ts - `describe("Traceability ESLint Plugin (Story 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP)")` - Verifies: - `rules` and `configs` are defined and objects. - `plugin.rules === rules` and `plugin.configs === configs`. - Tagged with: - `@story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md` - `@req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE`.
- Default export, rule registry, and configs: - tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts - Confirms default export wiring: - `[REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE] default export includes rules and configs` (plugin.rules/configs reference the same objects). - Validates rule registry contents: - `[REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE] rules object has correct rule names` → keys exactly: ["require-story-annotation", "require-req-annotation", "require-branch-annotation", "valid-annotation-format", "valid-story-reference", "valid-req-reference", "prefer-implements-annotation"]. - This proves a central registry of multiple validation rules is present (REQ-RULE-REGISTRY). - Validates config system: - `[REQ-RULE-REGISTRY] configs.recommended contains correct rule configuration` – ensures core rules are enabled. - `[REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM] configs.strict contains same rules as recommended`. - Validates error severity mapping (ties into error reporting story but also shows config design quality).
- Flat-config / ESLint v9 integration: - tests/config/flat-config-presets-integration.test.ts - Uses `FlatESLint` from `eslint/use-at-your-own-risk` (ESLint v9 flat config API). - Builds config as `[baseConfig, ...configs.recommended]` and `[baseConfig, ...configs.strict]`, where `baseConfig.plugins.traceability` is the plugin from src/index. - Verifies that linting `"function foo() {}"` under these configs produces messages that include `"traceability/require-story-annotation"`. - Requirements validated: - `[REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS] recommended preset enables traceability rules via documented usage`. - `[REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS] strict preset also enables traceability rules via documented usage`. - `[REQ-FLAT-CONFIG]` and overall ESLint v9 flat-config compatibility (supports REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT). - Project’s own ESLint flat config for development: eslint.config.js - Requires the plugin dynamically from either `./src/index.js` or `./lib/src/index.js`. - Integrates plugin via `plugins: { ...(plugin.rules ? { traceability: plugin } : {}) }` within flat-config blocks for JS/TS files. - Demonstrates real-world ESLint v9 flat-config integration used by this repo itself.
- CLI integration (end-to-end behavior via ESLint CLI): - tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts - Tagged for this story: `@story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md`, `@req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE - Validate plugin registers via CLI`. - Resolves ESLint CLI from installed `eslint` package and runs it with: - `--no-config-lookup --config --stdin --stdin-filename foo.js --rule ...`. - Parameterized tests ensure: - Missing `@story` → non-zero exit status under `traceability/require-story-annotation:error`. - Present `@story` with valid path → zero exit status. - Missing `@req` → non-zero exit under `traceability/require-req-annotation:error`. - Path traversal and absolute-path `@story`/`@req` combinations produce errors under `valid-req-reference`. - All these tests passed in the Jest run, proving the plugin loads and functions correctly in real ESLint CLI usage (Core Functionality + Integration).
- Error handling for plugin/rule loading: - Implementation in src/index.ts: - Dynamic rule load within RULE_NAMES.forEach uses `try { require('./rules/${name}') } catch (error) { ... }`. - On failure: - Logs to stderr: `[eslint-plugin-traceability] Failed to load rule "${name}": ${error.message}`. - Registers a placeholder `RuleModule` under `rules[name]` with: - `meta.docs.description: "Failed to load rule 'name'"`. - `create` that reports an ESLint error: `eslint-plugin-traceability: Error loading rule "${name}": ${error.message}`. - tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts - Mocks a rule module (`../src/rules/require-branch-annotation`) to throw on import. - Requires `../src/index` to force plugin initialization. - Asserts: - `console.error` called with message containing `Failed to load rule "require-branch-annotation": Test load error`. - `plugin.rules["require-branch-annotation"]` is defined and has `meta.docs.description` stating the failure. - Placeholder rule’s `create` reports a Program-level error that includes the load error message. - Tagged with `@req REQ-ERROR-HANDLING` for this story. - tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts - Runs ESLint CLI using the project’s eslint.config.js with the plugin. - Uses `spawnSync` to run Node with ESLint CLI over `"function foo() {}"` and `traceability/require-story-annotation:error`. - Asserts non-zero exit and that stdout contains the rule’s missing-annotation message; this ensures CLI surfaces plugin errors meaningfully. - Tagged with `@req REQ-ERROR-HANDLING`.
- NPM package structure and TypeScript setup: - package.json - "name": "eslint-plugin-traceability" (standard plugin naming convention). - "main": "lib/src/index.js" and "types": "lib/src/index.d.ts" (compiled TS output and type declarations). - "files": ["lib", "README.md", "LICENSE", "SECURITY.md", "user-docs", "CHANGELOG.md"] – ensures published package includes built plugin, docs, and license only. - "peerDependencies": { "eslint": "^9.0.0" } – explicitly declares ESLint v9 compatibility. - "engines": { "node": ">=18.18.0" } – runtime support constraints. - "scripts": includes `build`, `test` (jest), `type-check` (tsc), and lint/format/duplication scripts, satisfying REQ-TEST-SETUP. - Has `bin.traceability-maint` pointing to `lib/src/maintenance/cli.js` (CLI tool is outside this story’s scope but shows complete package wiring). - tsconfig.json - `module: "CommonJS"`, `outDir: "lib"`, `declaration: true`, `strict: true`, `esModuleInterop: true`. - `include: ["src", "tests"]` – both plugin and tests are in TypeScript, satisfying REQ-TYPESCRIPT and REQ-TEST-SETUP.
- User-facing documentation (install, configure, use): - README.md - Description: explains plugin purpose (traceability via @story/@req). - Attribution: "Created autonomously by voder.ai" with link. - Installation section: - `npm install --save-dev eslint-plugin-traceability` - `yarn add --dev eslint-plugin-traceability`. - Usage and configuration: - Provides full ESLint v9 flat-config example: ```js import js from "@eslint/js"; import traceability from "eslint-plugin-traceability";
export default [ js.configs.recommended, { plugins: { traceability }, }, ...traceability.configs.recommended, ]; ``` - Quick Start section also shows a minimal flat-config plus sample @story/@req annotation usage, and `npx eslint` invocation. - Documents available rules and where to find rule-specific docs (user-docs/*). - Mentions CLI integration and how to run tests, linking to more docs. - This fulfills the story’s "User Experience" and "Documentation" acceptance criteria: clear install and configuration instructions, including concrete ESLint v9 examples.
- Project-level ESLint flat-config usage (self-dogfooding): - eslint.config.js - Loads plugin from source or built lib and injects it into flat-config `plugins` blocks. - Configures TS and JS files with the plugin’s rules and other quality rules. - Demonstrates compatibility with ESLint v9 flat configuration in practice.
- Test execution (from `npm test -- --verbose`): - All relevant suites passed: - `tests/plugin-setup.test.ts` – "Traceability ESLint Plugin (Story 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP)". - `tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts` – "Plugin Default Export and Configs (Story 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP)". - `tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts` – "[docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md] CLI Integration (traceability plugin)". - `tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts` – "Traceability ESLint Plugin Error Handling (Story 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP)". - `tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts` – "CLI Error Handling for Traceability Plugin (Story 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP)". - Overall Jest summary: - Test Suites: 35 passed, 35 total - Tests: 266 passed, 266 total - All story-related tests for 001.0 passed without failure.
traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria and technical requirements for 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP are implemented and verified: - Core functionality: The plugin registers correctly, exports rules and configs, and loads under Node/ESLint without errors. This is validated by unit tests (plugin-setup.test.ts, plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts) and by end-to-end CLI integration tests with ESLint. - Quality standards: The plugin follows standard ESLint plugin patterns (default export with rules/configs, rule IDs under a namespace, flat-config-compatible presets, peer dependency on ESLint). TypeScript is used with a strict tsconfig, and the package is structured for publishing. - Integration with ESLint v9 flat config: Dedicated tests using FlatESLint and the documented presets confirm that `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict` work as flat-config snippets, and the project’s own eslint.config.js integrates the plugin using flat config. - User experience & documentation: README.md provides clear installation steps, flat-config examples, quick start, rule list, and references to further user docs, fulfilling the plugin setup/documentation expectations of the story. - Error handling: Dynamic rule loading in src/index.ts catches load failures, logs clear errors, and installs placeholder rules; tests confirm both module-level behavior and CLI-level error reporting. - NPM package, TypeScript, and test setup: package.json, tsconfig.json, and Jest tests (including CLI integration) show the plugin is a proper TypeScript-based, test-covered, publishable ESLint plugin package. Given the concrete implementation and passing tests directly tied to this story, the specification for docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md is fully satisfied.
